artworks.title: Telephus Seated on the Altar with Bandaged Thigh
artworks.description: Telephus on the altar with bandaged thigh — the Mysian king wounded by Achilles when the Achaeans mistook Mysia for Troy.

artworks.title: Telephus Threatening the Infant Orestes (Telephus Frieze, Panel 42)
artworks.description: The Pergamon Telephus frieze: Telephus threatens infant Orestes — the hostage bargain that forces Achilles to heal the wound he made.

artworks.title: Achilles Healing Telephus with the Rust of His Spear
artworks.description: Achilles heals Telephus with spear-rust — the oracle that only the wounder can cure, unlocking the fleet's road to Troy.

artworks.title: Telephus Frieze: Telephus receives weapons from Auge (Pergamon Altar, panels 16–17)
artworks.description: Telephus receives weapons from Auge on the Pergamon frieze — the Mysian hero armed before the Achaean clash.

popCulture.title: Telephus
popCulture.description: The spear that wounds must heal — Achilles' Pelian shaft, Euripides' lost beggar-king tragedy, and the Mysian guide to Troy.

popCulture.title: The Acharnians
popCulture.creator: Aristophanes
popCulture.description: Aristophanes' comedy keeps parodying Euripides' Telephus — the rags, the hostage infant, and the wound that only the spear can cure.

popCulture.title: Cypria
popCulture.description: The cyclic prequel lands the Achaeans in Mysia by mistake — Telephus' wound opens the road to Ilium.
